title: Last Bell, 2009
logline: One week before the wedding. The bell. Wood buys the thrift-store suit that afternoon. The strip draws the suit, not the bell.

panels.composition: A thrift store on main street, 3:05 PM. The bell through the window. WOOD holding a wool suit on a hanger up to himself. BARNABY.

characters.pose: holding a suit up to himself

image.prompt: a thin man in a thrift store holding a wool suit on a hanger up against himself, a bell sound drawn through the window, a dog, muddy flats

panels.composition: The suit. Gray wool. A smell drawn as faint wavy lines: mothballs.

image.prompt: close-up of a gray wool suit on a thrift-store hanger with faint wavy odor lines rising from it

balloons.text: Best man. Nine dollars. It smells like a closet somebody died in.

image.prompt: a man holding a suit and talking to a dog with dry resignation

panels.composition: Wood walking home up main street with the suit over his shoulder, the dog, the school letting out behind him. The bell, off-page.

image.prompt: a thin man walking up a small-town main street with a suit over his shoulder and an old dog beside him, students dispersing in the distance, no words

art.line: brush-pen; the flats cleaner; Sundays the point

notes: The suit: nine dollars, mothballs. It returns in 2014.
